claims.locator: PDF p.1, title, Abstract and publication header; pp.2–3, Introduction and Section 3
claims.passage: The title, authors and DOI match candidate W4398763293. The PDF gives online availability as 24 May 2024. The authors describe a review and critical analysis of 126 CSLR studies organized by sign language, acquisition, modality, cues, techniques, datasets and performance. CSLR is defined as recognizing successive signs in unsegmented video, distinct from isolated recognition.

Section 4.2.2 describes SubUNets (Camgoz et al., 2017), combining CNNs, BLSTMs and CTC with cropped-hand and full-frame images. Section 4.2.3 describes Cui et al. (2017), combining convolutional visual features, temporal convolutions and BLSTM. Table 8 labels both approaches as vision-based and compares their architectures and development/test WER on Phoenix2014. The two distinct CSLR studies satisfy the project-specific full-text comparison threshold.

The review covers visual RGB-based and multi-cue CSLR, including RGB CorrNet, a model combining pose/face/hands/full-frame features, and two-stream networks processing full frames and pose heatmaps. The presence of sensor-based studies elsewhere does not remove its qualifying vision-based coverage.

The authors organize research gaps into data-centric and model-centric issues. These include limited datasets and signing domains, naturalistic recording conditions, signer independence, non-manual cues, multimodal fusion and real-time efficiency. These are the review authors' assessments, not independently verified absences across the literature.

claims.passage: Section 7 discusses prior continuous-recognition methods. Section 7.1 describes Pu et al. (2018), combining 3D-ResNet, dilated CNN and CTC on RGB video; Section 7.3 describes Cui et al. (2019), combining CNN/Bi-LSTM, iterative training, RGB and optical flow. Table 8 compares their modalities, models, datasets and reported error rates, including PHOENIX-Weather 2014 and SIGNUM. These are two distinct prior CSLR studies.

The discussion distinguishes isolated recognition from sequence recognition and temporal alignment. It identifies feature extraction and alignment as central issues and proposes attention, multiple modalities, structured spatiotemporal models and sign-language prior knowledge as future directions. Table 8 includes visual RGB-video methods.
